metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: into this whole other field in my view, which is economics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: which I always thought was really boring,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: but we have no choice but to turn into economists

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: if we wanna fix this problem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: But I've been around this thing since it started,

body.input: and whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: What I'd like to argue is it's possible to strive

body.input: I think one way to do this is to try to look around

body.input: and see which ones have more healthy conversations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: One that I've been really interested in is GitHub.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Because it contains, I'm not saying it'll always be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: but for the most part, GitHub has had a relatively

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: quite low poison quotient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And I think there's a few things about GitHub

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that are interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: One thing about it is that people have a stake in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: It's not just empty status games.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: There's actual code or there's actual stuff being done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And I think as soon as you have a real world stake

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: in something, you have a motivation

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: to not screw up that thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And I think that that's often missing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that there's no incentive for the person

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: to really preserve something if they get a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: of attention from dumping on somebody's TikTok or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: They don't pay any price for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: But you have to kind of get decent with people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: when you have a shared stake, a little secret.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: So GitHub does a bit of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: GitHub is wonderful, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: But I'm tempted to play the Jaren Becka at you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: which is that GitHub is currently is amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: to manipulate you because you wanna preserve the stake.

body.input: So like.

body.input: Right, well this is why, this gets us into the economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: So there's this thing called data dignity

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that I've been studying for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I wrote a book about an earlier version of it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: called Who Owns the Future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And the basic idea of it is that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: once again, this is a 30 year conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: It's a fascinating topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Let me do the fastest version of this I can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: The fastest way I know how to do this

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: is to compare two futures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: All right, so future one is then the normative one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: the one we're building right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And then future two is gonna be data dignity, okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And I'm gonna use a particular population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I live on the hill in Berkeley.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And one of the features about the hill

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Like it's dangerous, and it didn't used to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And so who keeps us alive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Well, the city does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: The city does some things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: The electric company, kinda sort of, maybe hopefully better.

body.input: Individual people who own property,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: take care of their property, that's all nice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: But there's this other middle layer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: which is fascinating to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: which is that the groundskeepers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: who work up and down that hill,

body.input: many of whom are not legally here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: many of whom don't speak English,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: cooperate with each other to make sure trees don't touch

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: to transfer fire easily from lot to lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: They have this whole little web that's keeping us safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I didn't know about this at first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I just started talking to them

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: because they were out there during the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And so I try to just see who are these people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Who are these people who are keeping us alive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Now, I wanna talk about the two different traits

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: for those people under future one and future two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: Future one, some weird kindergarten paint job van

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: with all these cameras and weird things drives up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: observes what the gardeners and groundskeepers are doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: A few years later, some amazing robots

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that can shimmy up trees and all this show up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: All those people are out of work

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: and there are these robots doing the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: and the robots are good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And they can scale to more land and they're actually good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: But then there are all these people out of work

body.input: and these people have lost dignity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: They don't know what they're gonna do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And then somebody will say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: well, they go on basic income, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: They become wards of the state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: My problem with that solution is every time in history

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that you've had some centralized thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that's doling out the benefits,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that things get seized by people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: because it's too centralized and it gets seized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: This happened to every communist experiment I can find.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: So I think that turns into a poor future

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: that will be unstable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I don't think people will feel good in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: I think it'll be a political disaster

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: with a sequence of people seizing this central source

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: of the basic income.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: And you'll say, oh no, an algorithm can do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jaron Lanier: Virtual Reality, Social Media & the Future of Humans and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #218

body.input: You studied the development of the human brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: for many years, so let me ask you

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: an out of the box question first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: How likely is it that there's intelligent life out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: in the universe, outside of Earth,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: with something like the human brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So I can put it another way, how unlikely is the human brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: How difficult is it to build a thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: through the evolutionary process?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Well, it has happened here, right, on this planet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Once, yes. Once.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So that simply tells you that it could, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: happen again other places.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's only a matter of probability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: What the probability that you would get a brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: like the ones that we have, like the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So how difficult is it to make the human brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's pretty difficult, but most importantly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I guess we know very little about how this process

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: really happens, and there is a reason for that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: actually multiple reasons for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Most of what we know about how the mammalian brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: so the brain of mammals, develop, comes from studying

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: in labs other brains, not our own brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the brain of mice, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: But if I showed you a picture of a mouse brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and then you put it next to a picture of a human brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: they don't look at all like each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So they're very different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And therefore there is a limit to what you can learn about

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: how the human brain is made by studying the mouse brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: There is a huge value in studying the mouse brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: There are many things that we have learned,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: but it's not the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: In having studied the human brain, or through the mouse,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and through other methodologies that we'll talk about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: do you have a sense, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: you're one of the experts in the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: how much do you feel you know about the brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And how often do you find yourself in awe

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of this mysterious thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Yeah, you pretty much find yourself in awe all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's an amazing process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's a process by which, by means that we don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: fully understand, at the very beginning of embryogenesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the structure called the neural tube literally self-assembles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And it happens in an embryo,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and it can happen also from stem cells in a dish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And then from there, these stem cells that are present

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: within the neural tube give rise to all of the thousands

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and thousands of different cell types

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that are present in the brain through time, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: With the interesting, very intriguing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: interesting observation is that the time that it takes

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: for the human brain to be made, it's human time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Meaning that for me and you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: it took almost nine months of gestation to build the brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and then another 20 years of learning postnatally

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: to get the brain we have today

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that allows us to this conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: A mouse takes 20 days or so

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: for an embryo to be born.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And so the brain is built in a much shorter period of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And the beauty of it is that if you take mouse stem cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and you put them in a culture dish,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the brain organoid that you get from a mouse

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: is formed faster than if you took human stem cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and put them in the dish

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and let them make a human brain organoid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So the very developmental process is...

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Controlled by the speed of the species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Which means it's on purpose, it's not accidental,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: or there is something in that temporal dynamic

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: to that development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Exactly, that is very important for us to get the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: We have, and we can speculate for why that is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: You know, it takes us a long time as human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: After we're born to learn all the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that we have to learn to have the adult brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's actually 20 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: From when a baby is born to when a teenager

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: goes through puberty to adults, it's a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Do you think you can maybe talk through

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the first few months and then on to the first 20 years

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and then for the rest of their lives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: what is the development of the human brain look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: What are the different stages?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Yeah, at the beginning you have to build a brain, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And the brain is made of cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: What's the very beginning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Which beginning are we talking about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: In the embryo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: As the embryo is developing in the womb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: in addition to making all of the other tissues

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of the embryo, the muscle, the heart, the blood,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the embryo is also building the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And it builds from a very simple structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: called the neural tube,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: which is basically nothing but a tube of cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that spans sort of the length of the embryo

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: from the head all the way to the tail,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: let's say, of the embryo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And then over in human beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: over many months of gestation, from that neural tube,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: which contains stem cell-like cells of the brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: you will make many, many other building blocks of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So all of the other cell types,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: because there are many, many different types of cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: in the brain that will form specific structures of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So you can think about embryonic development of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: as just the time in which you are making

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the building blocks, the cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Are the stem cells relatively homogeneous, like uniform,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: or are they all different?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: That's a very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's exactly how it works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: You start with a more homogeneous,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: perhaps more multipotent type of stem cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: What's multipotent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Multipotent means that it has the potential

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: to make many, many different types of other cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And then with time, these progenitors

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: become more heterogeneous, which means more diverse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: There are gonna be many different types of the stem cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And also they will give rise to progeny, to other cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that are not stem cells, that are specific cells of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that are very different from the mother stem cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And now you think about this process of making cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: from the stem cells over many, many months

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of development for humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And what you're doing here, building the cells

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of the community, how difficult is it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Is it truly science fiction at this point?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I think the field will progress, like I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that really are built out of understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of how this process really works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And it's hard to predict how complex this really will be.

body.input: I really don't think we're so far from,

body.input: that is always a bad version of it,

body.input: but that may have really powerful properties.

body.input: And might be able to respond to stimuli

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: or be used in certain contexts.

body.input: we can talk about science fiction and write that book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and we could today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: But this work happens in a specific ethical framework

body.input: that we don't decide just as scientists,

body.input: So the ethical framework here is a fascinating one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: or at least start to cure by understanding it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Every discussion about the ethics of this

body.input: needs to be based on actual data

body.input: from the models that we have today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and from the ones that we will have tomorrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So that's the way to think about the ethics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I also learned that what you do for them comes back to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Like, if you're a good parent, you're going to, most of the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: have perhaps a decent kids at the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So what do you think, just a quick comment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: what do you think is the source of that difference?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: That's often the surprising thing for parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: They can't believe that our kids, they're so different,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: yet they came from the same parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Well, they are genetically different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Even they came from the same two parents because the mixing of gametes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: we know this genetics, creates every time a genetically different individual,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: which will have a specific mix of genes that is a different mix every time

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: from the two parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And so they're not twins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: They are genetically different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Even just that little bit of variation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Because you said, really, from a biological perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the brains look pretty similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Well, so let me clarify that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So the genetics you have, the genes that you have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that play that beautiful orchestrated symphony of development,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: different genes will play it slightly differently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's like playing the same piece of music,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: but with a different orchestra and a different director.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: The music will not come out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It will be still a piece by the same author,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: but it will come out differently if it's played by the high school

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: orchestra instead of the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Instead of La Scala in Milan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And so you are born superficially with the same brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It has the same cell types, similar patterns of connectivity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: but the properties of the cells and how the cells will then

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: react to the environment as you experience your world

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: will be also shaped by who genetically you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Speaking just as a parent, this is not something that comes from my work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I think you can tell at birth that these kids are different,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that they have a different personality in a way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So both is needed, the genetics as well as the nurturing afterwards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So you are one human with a brain, sort of living through the whole mess of it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the human condition, full of love, maybe fear, ultimately mortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: How has studying the brain changed the way you see yourself?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: When you look in the mirror, when you think about your life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the fears, the love, when you see your own life, your own mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Yeah, that's a very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's almost impossible to dissociate some time for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Some of the things we do or some of the things that other people do from,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: oh, that's because that part of the brain is working in a certain way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Or thinking about a teenager, going through teenage years

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and being at times funny in the way they think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And impossible for me not to think it's because they're going through

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: this period of time called critical periods of plasticity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: where their synapses are being eliminated here and there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and they're just confused.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And so from that comes perhaps a different take on that behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: or maybe I can justify it scientifically in some sort of way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I also look at humanity in general, and I am amazed by what we can do

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and the kind of ideas that we can come up with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And I cannot stop thinking about how the brain is continuing to evolve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: I don't know if you do this, but I think about the next brain sometimes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Where are we going with this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: What are the features of this brain that evolution is really playing with

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: to get us in the future the new brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's not over, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's a work in progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So let me just a quick comment on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Do you think there's a lot of fascination and hope for artificial intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: of creating artificial brains?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: You said the next brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: When you imagine over a period of a thousand years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the evolution of the human brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: do you sometimes envisioning that future see an artificial one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Artificial intelligence as it is hoped by many, not hoped,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: thought by many people would be actually the next evolutionary step

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: in the development of humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Yeah, I think in a way that will happen, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It's almost like a part of the way we evolve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: We evolve in the world that we created, that we interact with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: that shape us as we grow up and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Sometimes I think about something that may sound silly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: but think about the use of cell phones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Part of me thinks that somehow in their brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: there will be a region of the cortex that is attuned to that tool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And this comes from a lot of studies in model organisms

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: where really the cortex especially adapts to the kind of things you have to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So if we need to move our fingers in a very specific way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: we have a part of our cortex that allows us to do this kind of very precise movement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: An owl that has to see very, very far away with big eyes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the visual cortex very big, the brain attunes to your environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So the brain will attune to the technologies that we will have and will be shaped by it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So the cortex very well may be shaped by it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: In artificial intelligence, it may merge with it, it may get enveloped and adjusted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Even if it's not a merge of the kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: oh, let's have a synthetic element together with a biological one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: The very space around us, the fact, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: think about we put on some goggles of virtual reality

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: and we physically are surfing the ocean, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Like I've done it and you have all these emotions that come to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Your brain placed you in that reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And it was able to do it like that just by putting the goggles on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: It didn't take thousands of years of adapting to this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: The brain is plastic, so adapts to new technology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So you could do it from the outside by simply hijacking some sensory capacities that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So clearly over recent evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: the cerebral cortex has been a part of the brain that has known the most evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So we have put a lot of chips on evolving this specific part of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: And the evolution of cortex is plasticity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: is this ability to change in response to things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: So, yes, they will integrate, that we want it or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Paola Arlotta: Brain Development from Stem Cell to Organoid | Lex Fridman Podcast #32

body.input: Well, there's no better way to end it.

body.input: They're a last remnant of a very, very old way of doing simple transactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: coins are generic and fungible. They can be used in any transaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That was an important evolutionary advance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: If you think of financial history, and this was the point of the Ascent of Money, as an evolutionary story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: there are punctuated equilibria. People get by with coins for a long time, despite their defects as a means of payment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: such as that they can be debased, they can be clipped. It's very hard to avoid fake or debased money entering the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But coinage is still kind of the basis of payments all the way through the Roman Empire, out the other end into the so-called Dark Ages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's still how most things are settled in cash transactions in the early 1300s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You don't get a big shift until after the Black Death, when there is such a need to monetize the economy

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: because of chronic labor shortages and feudalism begins to unravel, that you just don't have a sufficient amount of coinage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You get bills of exchange. I'm really into bills of exchange because, and this I hope will capture your listeners' and viewers' imaginations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: when they start using bills of exchange, which are really just pieces of paper saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I owe you over a three-month period while goods are in transit from Florence to London,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: you get the first peer-to-peer payment system, which is network verified because they're not coins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They don't have a king's head on them. They're just pieces of paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The verification comes in the form of signatures. You need, ultimately, some kind of guarantee.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: If I write an IOU to you, Bill, you don't really know me that well. We only just met.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You might want to get endorsed by, I don't know, somebody really credit-worthy like Elon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We actually can see in the late 14th century in northern Italy, in England, and elsewhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: the evolution of a peer-to-peer network system of payment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's actually how world trade grows because you just couldn't settle long oceanic transactions with coinage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It just wasn't practical. All those treasure chests full of doubloons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: which were part of the way in which the Spanish Empire worked, were really inefficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So bills of exchange are an exciting part of the story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: and they illustrate something I should have made more clear with the ascent of money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: that not everything used in payment needs to be money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Classically, economists will tell you, oh, well, money. Money has three different functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You've heard this a zillion times, right? It's a unit of account. It's a store of value, and it's a medium of exchange.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Now, there are three or four things that are worth saying about this, and I'll just say two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: One, it may be that those three things are a trilemma, and it's very difficult for anything to be all of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: This point was made by my Hoover colleague, Manny Rincon-Cruz, last year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: and I still wish he would write this up as a paper because it's a great insight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The second thing that's really interesting to me is that payments don't need to be money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And if we go around, as economists love to do, saying, well, Bitcoin's not money because it doesn't fulfill these criteria,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: we're missing the point that you could build a system of payments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: which I think is how we should think about crypto, that isn't money, doesn't need to be money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's like bills of exchange. It's network-based verification, peer-to-peer transactions without third-party verification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: When it hit me the other day that we actually have this precedent for crypto, I got quite excited and thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I wish I had written that in the Ascent of Money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Can you, from a first principles, almost like a physics perspective or maybe a human perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: describe where does the value of money come from? Where is it actually? Where is it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So it's a sheet of paper or it's coins, but it feels like in a platonic sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: there's some kind of thing that's actually storing the value, as us, a bunch of ants are dancing around and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I come from a family of physicists. I'm the black sheep of the family. My mother's a physicist, my sister is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so when you ask me to explain something in physics terms, I get a kind of little part of me dies because I know I'll fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But in truth, it doesn't really matter what we decide money is going to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Anything can record, crystallize the relationship between the creditor and the debtor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It can be a piece of paper. It can be a piece of metal. It can be nothing. It can just be a digital entry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's trust that we're really talking about here. We are not just trusting one another. We may not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But we are trusting the money. So whatever we use to represent the creditor-debtor relationship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: whether it's a banknote or a coin or whatever, it does depend on us both trusting it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that doesn't always pertain. What we see in episodes of inflation, especially episodes of hyperinflation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: is a crisis of trust, a crisis of confidence in the means of payment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And this is very traumatic for the societies to which it happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: By and large, human beings, particularly once you have a rule of law system of the sort that evolved in the West and then became generalized,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: are predisposed to trust one another. And the default setting is to trust money,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: even when it depreciates at a quite steady rate, as the US dollar has done pretty much uninterruptedly since the 1960s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It takes quite a big disruption for money to lose that trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But I think essentially what money should be thought of as is a series of tokens that can take any form we like and can be purely digital,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: which represent our transactions as creditors and debtors. And the whole thing depends on our collective trust to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I had to explain this to Stephen Colbert once in the Colbert show, the old show that was actually funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It was a great moment when he said, so, Neil, could I be money?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I said, yes, we could. We could settle a debt with a human being that was quite common in much of history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But it's not the most convenient form of money. Money has to be convenient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's why when they worked out how to make payments with cell phones, the Chinese simply went straight there from bank accounts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They skipped out credit cards. You won't see credit cards in China, except in the hands of naive tourists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: How much can this trust bear in terms of us humans with our human nature testing it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I guess the surprising thing is the thing works. A bunch of self-interested ants running around trading in trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it seems to work except for a bunch of moments in human history when there's hyperinflation, like you mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it's just kind of amazing. It's kind of amazing that us humans, if I were to be optimistic and sort of hopeful about human nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: it gives me a sense that people want to lean on each other. They want to trust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's certainly, I would say, probably now a widely shared view amongst evolutionary psychologists, network scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: One of Nicholas Christakis' argument in a recent book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239
