metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It sounds like you put quite a bit of a blame on the man, Chamberlain, and give credit to somebody like a Churchill.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What is the difference? Where's that line?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You've also written a book about Henry Kissinger, who's an interesting person that's been throughout many difficult decisions in the games of power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What does it take to be a great leader in that moment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That particular moment, sorry to keep talking, is fascinating to me because it feels like it's man-on-man conversations that define history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Hitler was bluffing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He really wasn't ready for war in 1938.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The German economy was clearly not ready for war in 1938.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Chamberlain made a fundamental miscalculation along with his advisors because it wasn't all Chamberlain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He was in many ways articulating the establishment view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I tried to show in a book called War of the World how that establishment worked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It extended through the BBC into the aristocracy to Oxford.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: There was an establishment view. Chamberlain personified it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Churchill was seen as a warmonger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He was at his lowest point of popularity in 1938.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But what is it that Chamberlain gets wrong?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Because it's conceptual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Chamberlain is persuaded that Britain has to play for time because Britain is not ready for war in 1938.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He fails to see that the time that he gets, that he buys at Munich, is also available to Hitler.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Everybody gets the time and Hitler is able to do much more with it because Hitler strikes the pact with Stalin

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: that guarantees that Germany can fight a war on one front in 1939.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What does Chamberlain do? Build some more aircraft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The great mistake of the strategy of appeasement was to play for time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I mean, they knew war was coming, but they were playing for time, not realizing that Hitler got the time too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And after he partitioned Czechoslovakia, he was in a much stronger position,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: not least because of all the resources that they were able to plunder from Czechoslovakia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So that was the conceptual mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Churchill played an heroic role in pointing out this mistake and predicting accurately that it would lead to war on worse terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What does it take? It takes a distinct courage to be unpopular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And Churchill was deeply unpopular at that point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: People would listen to him in the House of Commons in silence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: On one occasion, Lady Astor shouted, rubbish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So he went through a period of being hated on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The other thing that made Churchill a formidable leader was that he always applied history to the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that's why he gets it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He sees the historical problem much more clearly than Chamberlain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So I think if you go back to 1938, there's no realistic counterfactual in which Churchill's in government in 1938.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You have to have France collapse for Churchill to come into government.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But you can certainly imagine a Tory elite that's thinking more clearly about the likely dynamics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They haven't seen this, I guess, problem of conjecture to take a phrase from Kissinger,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: which is that whatever they're doing in postponing the war has the potential to create a worse starting point for the war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It would have been risky in 1938, but it was a way better situation than they ended up with in 1939, a year later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You asked about Kissinger, and I've learned a lot from reading Kissinger and talking to Kissinger since I embarked on writing his biography a great many years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think one of the most important things I've learned is that you can apply history to contemporary problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It may be the most important tool that we have in that kind of decision making.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You have to do it quite ruthlessly and rigorously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And in the moment of crisis, you have to take risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So Kissinger often says in his early work, the temptation of the bureaucrat is to wait for more data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But ultimately, the decision making that we do under uncertainty can't be based on data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The problem of conjecture is that you could take an action now and incur some cost, an overt disaster,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: but you'll get no thanks for it because nobody is grateful for an averted disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Nobody goes around saying, wasn't it wonderful how we didn't have another 9-11?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: On the other hand, you can do nothing, incur no upfront costs and hope for the best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And you might get lucky, the disaster might not happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's in a democratic system, the much easier path to take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think the essence of leadership is to be ready to take that upfront cost, avert the disaster, and accept that you won't get gratitude.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: If I may make a comment, an aside about Henry Kissinger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So he, I think at 98 years old currently, has still got it. He's brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's very, very impressive. I can only hope that my brain has the same durability that his does,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: because it's a formidable intellect and it's still in as sharp form as it was 50 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So you mentioned Eric Schmidt's and his book, and they reached out to me that they want to do this podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I know Eric Schmidt, I've spoken to him before. I like him a lot, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So they said we could do a podcast for 40 minutes with Eric, 40 minutes with Eric and Henry together, and 40 minutes with Henry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So there's a three different conversations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I had to like, I had to do some soul searching because I said, fine, 40 minutes with Eric.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We'll probably talk many times again. Fine. Let's talk about this AI book together for 40 minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But I said, what I wrote to them is that I would hate myself if I only have 40 minutes to talk to Henry Kissinger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so I had to hold my ground, went back and forth, and in the end decided to part ways over this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I sometimes think about this kind of difficult decision in the podcasting space of when do you walk away?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Because there's a particular world leader that I've mentioned in the past where the conversation is very likely to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And as it happens, those conversations can often be, you know, unfortunately, this person only has 30 minutes now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I know we agreed for three hours, but unfortunately, and you have to decide, do I stand my ground on this on this point?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I suppose that's the thing that journalists have to think about, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Like, do I hold on to my integrity in whatever form that takes and do I stay my ground even if I lose a fascinating opportunity?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Anyway, something I thought about and something I think about and with Henry Kissinger, I mean, he's had a million amazing conversations in your biography.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So it's not like something is lost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But it was still nevertheless to me some soul searching that I had to do as a kind of practice for what to me is a higher stakes conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I'll just mention is Vladimir Putin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I can have a conversation with him unlike any conversation he's ever had, partially because I'm a fluent Russian speaker,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: partially because I'm messed up in the head in certain kind of ways that make for an interesting dynamic because we're both judo people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We both are certain kinds of human beings that can have a much deeper apolitical conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I have to ask to stay on the topic of leadership.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You've in your book, Doom, have talked about wars, pandemics throughout human history and in some sense saying that all of these disasters are manmade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So humans have a role in terms of the magnitude of the effect that they have on human civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Without taking cheap political shots, can we talk about COVID-19?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: How will history remember the COVID-19 pandemic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What were the successes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What were the failures of leadership of man, of humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Doom was a book that I was planning to write before the pandemic struck as a history of the future based in large measure on science fiction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It had occurred to me in 2019 that I had spent too long not reading science fiction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so I decided I would liven up my intake by getting off history for a bit and reading science fiction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Because history is great at telling you about the perennial problems of power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Putin is always interesting on history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He's become something of a historian recently with his essays and lectures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But what history is bad at telling you is, well, what will the effects of discontinuity of technology be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so I thought I need some science fiction to think more about this because I'm tending to miss the importance of technological discontinuity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: If you read a lot of science fiction, you read a lot of plague books because science fiction writers are really quite fond of the plague scenario.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So the world ends in many ways in science fiction, but one of the most popular is the lethal pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So when the first email came to me, I think it was on January the 3rd from my medical friend, Justin Stebbing, funny pneumonia in Wuhan, my antennae began to tingle because it was just like one of those science fiction books that begins in just that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: In a pandemic, as Larry Brilliant, the epidemiologist said many years ago, the key is early detection and early action.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's how you deal with a novel pathogen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And almost no Western country did that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We know it was doable because the Taiwanese and the South Koreans did it and they did it very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But really no Western country got this right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Some were unlucky because super spreader events happened earlier than in other countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Italy was hit very hard very early.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: For other countries, the real disaster came quite late.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Russia, which has only relatively recently had a really bad experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The lesson for me is quite different from the one that most journalists thought they were learning last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Most journalists last year thought Trump is a terrible president.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He's saying a lot of crazy things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's his fault that we have high excess mortality in the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The same argument was being made by journalists in Britain, Boris Johnson, dot, dot, dot, Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro, dot, dot, dot, even India, Narendra Modi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The same argument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think this argument is wrong in a few ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's true that the populist leaders said many crazy things and, broadly speaking, gave poor guidance to their populations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But I don't think it's true to say that with different leaders, these countries would have done significantly better if Joe Biden had magically been president a year earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I don't think the US would have done much better because the things that caused excess mortality last year weren't presidential decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They were utter failure of CDC to provide testing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That definitely wasn't Trump's fault.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Scott Gottlieb's book makes that very clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's just been published recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We utterly failed to use technology for contact tracing, which the Koreans did very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We didn't really quarantine anybody seriously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: There was no enforcement of quarantine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And we exposed the elderly to the virus as quickly as possible in elderly care homes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And these things have very little to do with presidential incompetence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So I think leadership is of somewhat marginal importance in a crisis like this because what you really need is your public health bureaucracy to get it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And very few Western public health bureaucracies got it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Could the president have given better leadership?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: His correct strategy, however, was to learn from Barack Obama's playbook with the opioid epidemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The opioid epidemic killed as many people on Obama's watch as COVID did on Trump's watch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it was worse in a sense because it only happened in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And each year it killed more people than the year before, over eight years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Nobody, to my knowledge, has ever seriously blamed Obama for the opioid epidemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Trump's mistake was to put himself front and center of the response to claim that he had some unique insight into the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And to say with every passing week more and more foolish things until even a significant portion of people who'd voted for him in 2016 realized that he'd blown it, which was why he lost the election.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The correct strategy was actually to make Mike Pence the pandemic czar and get the hell out of the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's what my advice to Trump would have been. In fact, it was in February of last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So the mistake was to try to lead. But actually, leadership in a pandemic is almost a contradiction in terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What you really need is your public health bureaucracy not to fuck it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And they really, really fucked it up. And that was then all blamed on Trump.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You know, Jim Fallows writes a piece in The Atlantic that says, well, being the president's like flying a light aircraft, it's pilot error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I read that piece and I thought, does he really after all the years he spent writing think that being president is like flying a light aircraft?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I mean, it's really nothing like flying a light aircraft. Being president is you sit on top of a vast bureaucracy with how many different agencies?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: 60, 70, we've all lost count. And you're surrounded by advisors, at least a quarter of whom are saying this is a disaster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We have to close the borders. And the others are saying, no, no, we have to keep the economy going.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's what you're running on in November.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So being a president in a pandemic is a very unenviable position because you actually can't you can't really determine whether your public health bureaucracy will get it right or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You don't think to push back on that, just like being Churchill in a war is difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So leaving Trump and Biden aside, what I would love to see from a president is somebody who makes great speeches and arouses the public to push the bureaucracy, the public health bureaucracy to get their shit together, to fire certain kinds of people to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I mean, I'm sorry, but I'm a big fan of powerful speeches, especially in the modern age with the Internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It can really move people. Instead, the lack of speeches resulted in certain kinds of forces amplifying division over whether to wear masks or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's like it's almost like the public picked some random topic over which to divide themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And there was like a complete indecision, which is really what it was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Fear of the of uncertainty materializing itself in some kind of division. And then you almost like busy yourself with the red versus blue politics as opposed to some I don't know FDR type character just stands and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Fuck all this bullshit that we're hearing. We're going to manufacture five billion tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: This is what America is great at. We're going to build the greatest testing infrastructure ever built or something or even with the vaccine development.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But that was what I was about to interject. Yes. In a pandemic, the most important thing is the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: If you get that right, then you should be forgiven for much else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that was the one thing the Trump administration got right because they went around the bureaucracy with Operation Warp Speed and achieved a really major success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So I think the paradox of the 2020 story in the United States is that the one thing that mattered most, the Trump administration got right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it got so much else wrong that was sort of marginal that we were left with the impression that Trump had been to blame for the whole disaster, which wasn't really quite right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Sure, it would have been great if we did Operation Warp Speed for testing, but ultimately vaccines are more important than tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And this brings me to the question that that you raised there of polarization and why that happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Now, in a book called The Square and the Tower, I argued that it would be very costly for the United States to allow the public sphere to continue to be dominated by a handful of big tech companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That this ultimately would have more adverse effects than simply contested elections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think we saw over the past 18 months just how bad this could be because the odd thing about this country is that we came up with vaccines with 90 plus percent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Efficacy and about 20 percent of people refuse to get them and still do refuse for reasons that seem best explained in terms of the anti-vax network, which has been embedded on the Internet for a long time, predating the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Rene de Resta wrote about this pre-2020, and this anti-vax network has turned out to kill maybe 200,000 Americans who could have been vaccinated but were persuaded through magical thinking that the vaccine was riskier than the virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Whereas you don't need to be an epidemiologist, you don't need to be a medical scientist to know that the virus is about two orders of magnitude riskier than the vaccine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So again, leadership could definitely have been better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But the politicization of everything was not Trump's doing alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It happened because our public sphere has been dominated by a handful of platforms whose business model inherently promotes polarization, inherently promotes fake news and extreme views,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: because those are the things that get the eyeballs on the screens and sell the ads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I mean, this is now a commonplace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But when one thinks about the cost of allowing this kind of thing to happen, it's now a very high human cost.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And we were foolish to leave uncorrected these structural problems in the public sphere that were already very clearly visible in 2016.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And you described that, like you mentioned, that there's these networks that are almost like laying dormant, waiting for their time in the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And they stepped forward in this case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that those network effects just serve as catalyst for whatever the bad parts of human nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I do hope that there's kinds of networks that emphasize the better angels of our nature, to quote Steven Pinker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's just clearly, and we know this from all the revelations of the Facebook whistleblower,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: there is clearly a very clear tension between the business model of a company like Facebook and the public good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And they know that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I just talked to the founder of Instagram.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yes, that's the case, but it's not, from a technology perspective, like absolutely true of any kind of social network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think it's possible to build, actually, I think it's not just possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think it's pretty easy if you set that as the goal, to build social networks that don't have these negative effects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Right. But if the business model is we sell ads and the way you sell ads is to maximize user engagement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: then the algorithm is biased in favor of fake news and extreme views.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So it's not the ads. A lot of people blame the ads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The problem, I think, is the engagement, and the engagement is just the easiest, the dumbest way to sell the ads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think there's much different metrics that could be used to make a lot more money than the engagement in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It has more to do with planning for the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So optimizing the selling of ads to make people happy with themselves in the long term, as opposed to some kind of addicted, like dopamine feeling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so that's, to me, that has to do with metrics and measuring things correctly and sort of also creating a culture with what's valued,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: to have difficult conversations about what we're doing with society, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think once you have those conversations, this takes us back to the University of Austin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: once you have those difficult human conversations, you can design the technology that will actually make for help people grow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: become the best version of themselves, help them be happy in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What gives you hope about the future?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: As somebody who studies some of the darker moments of human history, what gives you hope?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: A couple of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: First of all, the United States has a very unique operating system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: which was very well designed by the founders who'd thought a lot about history and realized it would take quite a novel design to prevent the Republic going the way of all republics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: because republics tend to end up as tyrannies for reasons that were well established by the time of the Renaissance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it gives me hope that this design has worked very well and withstood an enormous stress test in the last year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I became an American in 2018.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think one of the most important features of this operating system is that it is the magnet for talent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Here we sit, part of the immigration story in a darkened room with funny accents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Scott in a Russian walk into a recording studio and talk about America.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's very much like a joke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And Elon's a South African and so on, and Teal is a German.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We're extraordinarily fortunate that the natives let us come and play in a way that we could not in our countries of birth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And as long as the United States continues to exploit that superpower, that it is the talent magnet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: then it should out innovate the totalitarian competition every time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So that's one reason for being an optimist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Another reason, and it's quite a historical reason, as you would expect from me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: another reason that I'm optimistic is that my kids give me a great deal of hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They range in age from 27 down to four.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But each of them in their different way seems to be finding a way through this crazy time of ours without losing contact with that culture and civilization that I hold dear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I don't want to live in the metaverse as Mark Zuckerberg imagines it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: To me, that's a kind of ghastly hell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think Western civilization is the best civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think that almost all the truths about the human condition can be found in Western literature, art, and music.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think also that the civilization that produced the scientific revolution has produced the great problem solving tool that eluded the other civilizations that never really cracked science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And what gives me hope is that despite all the temptations and distractions that their generation had to contend with, my children in their different ways have found their way to literature and to art and to music.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And they are civilized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I don't claim much of the credit for that. I've done my best. But I think it's deeply encouraging that they found their way to the things that I think are indispensable for a happy life, a fulfilled life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Nobody, I think, can be truly fulfilled if they're cut off from the great body of Western literature, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I've thought a lot about Elon's argument that we might be in a simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: No, no, there is a simulation. It's called literature. And we just have to decide whether or not to enter it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I'm currently in the midst of the later stages of Proust's great A L'Encheure du Temps Perdus. And Proust's observation of human relationships is perhaps more meticulous than that of any other writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it's impossible not to find yourself identifying with Marcel and his obsessive, jealous relationships, particularly with Albertine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's the simulation. And you decide, I think, as a sentient being, how far to, in your own life, reenact these more profound experiences that others have written down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: One of my earliest literary simulations was to reenact Jack Kerouac's trip in On the Road when I was 17, culminating in getting very wasted in the hanging gardens of Zocchimilco, not to be missed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it hit me just as I was reading Proust, that that's really how to live a rich life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That one lives life, but one lives it juxtaposing one's own experience against the more refined experiences of the great writers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So it gives me hope that my children do that a bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Do you include the Russian authors in the canon?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yes, I don't read Russian, but I was entirely obsessed with Russian literature as a schoolboy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I read my way through Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Turgenev, Tchaikov.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think of all of those writers, Tolstoy had the biggest impact because at the end of War and Peace, there's this great essay on historical determinism, which I think was the reason I became a historian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But I'm really temperamentally a kind of Turgenev person, oddly enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think if you haven't read those novelists, I mean, you can't really be a complete human being if you haven't read the brothers Karamazov.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You're not grown up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so I think in many ways, those are the greatest novels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Raskolnikov's, remember Raskolnikov's nightmare at the end of Crime and Punishment, in which he imagines in his dream, a world in which a terrible virus spreads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Do you remember this? And this virus has the effect of making every individual think that what he believes is right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And in this self-righteousness, people fall on one another and commit appalling violence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's Raskolnikov's nightmare. And it's a prophecy. It's a terrible prophecy of Russia's future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yeah, and coupled with that is probably the, I also like the French, the existentialist, all that, the full spectrum when Germans, Hermann Hesse, and just that range of human thought as expressed in the literature is fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I really love your idea that the simulation, like one way to live life is to kind of explore these other worlds and borrow from them wisdom that you then just map onto your own life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You almost like stitch together your life with these kind of pieces from literature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The highly educated person is constantly struck by illusion. Everything is an illusion to something that one has read.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that is the simulation. That's what the real metaverse is. It's the imaginary world that we enter when we read, empathize, and then recognize in our daily lives some scrap of the shared experience that literature gives us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yeah, I think I've aspired to be the idiot from Prince Mishkin from Dostoevsky. And in aspiring to be that, I have become the idiot, I feel, at least in part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: What you mentioned the human condition, does love have to do? What role does it play in the human condition? Friendship, love?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Love is the drug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: This was a great Roxy music line that Brian Ferry wrote. And love is the most powerful and dangerous of all the drugs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The driving force that overrides our reason. And of course, it is the primal urge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So what a civilized society has to do is to prevent that drug, that primal force from creating mayhem. So there have to be rules like monogamy and rituals like marriage that reign love in and make the addict at least more or less under control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think that's part of why I'm a romantic rather than a Steve Pinker enlightenment rationalist. Because the romantics realized that love was the drug.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It's like the difference in sensibility between Handel and Wagner. And I had a Wagnerian phase when I was an undergraduate. I still remember thinking that in as old as Liebes toad that Wagner had got the closest to sex that anybody had ever got in music or perhaps to love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I'm lucky that I love my wife and that we were, by the time we met, smart enough to understand that love is a drug that you have to take in certain careful ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that it works best in the context of a stable family. That's the key thing. That one has to sort of take the drug and then submit to the conventions of marriage and family life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think in that respect, I'm a kind of tamed romantic. That's how I'd like to think of myself. And the degree to which your romanticism is tamed can be then channeled into productive work. That's why you're a historian and a writer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The rest of that love is channeled through the writing. So if you're going to be addicted to anything, be addicted to work. I mean, we're all addictive. But the thing about workaholism is that it is the most productive addiction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And rather that than drugs or booze. So yes, I'm always trying to channel my anxieties into work. I learned that at a relatively early age, it's a sort of massively productive way of coping with the inner demons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And again, we should teach kids that. Because let's come back to our earlier conversation about universities. Part of what happens at universities is that adolescents have to overcome all the inner demons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And these include deep insecurity about one's appearance, about one's intellect, and then madly raging hormones that cause you to behave like a complete fool with the people to whom you're sexually attracted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: All of this is going on in the university. How can it be a safe space? It's a completely dangerous space by definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So yeah, I learned teaching young people how to manage these storms. That's part of the job. And we're really not allowed to do that anymore because we can't talk about these things for fear of the Title IX officers kicking down the door and dragging us off in chains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And like you said, hard work and something you call work ethic in civilization is a pretty effective way to achieve, I think, a kind of happiness in a world that's full of anxiety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Or at least exhaustion so you sleep well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Well, there is beauty to the exhaustion. That's why running this manual work that some part of us is built for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Right. I mean, we are products of evolution and our adaptation to a technological world is a very imperfect one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So hence the kind of masochistic urge to run. I like outdoor exercise. I don't really like gyms. So I'll go for long punishing runs in Woodland, hike up hills. I like swimming in lakes and in the sea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Because that just has to be that physical activity in order to do the good mental work. And so it's all about trying to do the best work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: That's my sense that we have some random allocation of talent. You kind of figure out what it is that you're relatively good at and you try to do that well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I think my father encouraged me to think that way. And you don't mind about being average at the other stuff. The kind of sick thing is to try to be brilliant at everything. I hate those people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: You should really not worry too much if you're just an average double bass player, which I am, or kind of average skier, which I definitely am.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Doing those things okay is part of leading a rich and fulfilling life. I was not a good actor, but I got a lot out of acting as an undergraduate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It turned out after three years of experimentation at Oxford that I was, broadly speaking, better at writing history essays than my peers. And that was my edge. That was my comparative advantage. And so I've just tried to make a living from that slight edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yeah, that's a beautiful way to describe a life. Is there a meaning to this thing? Is there a meaning to life? What is the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I was brought up by a physicist and a physician. They were more or less committed atheists who had left the Church of Scotland as a protest against sectarianism in Glasgow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so my sister and I were told from an early age life was a cosmic accident. And that was it. There was no great meaning to it. And I can't really get past that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Isn't there a beauty to being an accident at a cosmic scale?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Yes, I wasn't taught to feel negative about that. And if anything, it was a frivolous insight. The whole thing was a kind of joke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And I think that atheism isn't really a basis for ordering a society, but it's been alright for me. I don't have a sense of a missing religious faith. For me, however, there's clearly some embedded Christian ethics in the way my parents lived.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So we were kind of atheist Calvinists who had kind of deposed God but carried on behaving as if we were members of the elect in a moral universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So that's kind of the state of mind that I was left in. And I think that we aren't really around long enough to claim that our individual lives have meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: But what Edmund Burke said is true. The real social contract is between the generations, between the dead, the living, and the unborn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And the meaning of life is, for me at least, to live in a way that honors the dead, seeks to learn from their accumulated wisdom because they do still outnumber us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They outnumber the living by quite a significant margin. And then to be mindful of the unborn and our responsibility to them. Writing books is a way of communicating with the unborn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It may or may not succeed, and probably won't succeed if my books are never assigned by woke professors in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So what we have to do is more than just write books and record podcasts. There have to be institutions. I'm 57 now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: I realized recently that succession planning had to be the main focus of the next 20 years because there are things that I really care about that I want future generations to have access to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so the meaning of life I do regard as being intergenerational transfer of wisdom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Ultimately, the species will go extinct at some point. Even if we do colonize Mars, one senses that physics will catch up with this particular organism, but it's in the pretty far distant future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And so the meaning of life is to make sure that for as long as there are human beings, they are able to live the kind of fulfilled lives, ethically fulfilled, intellectually fulfilled, emotionally fulfilled lives that civilization has made possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It would be easy for us to revert to the uncivilized world. There's a fantastic book that I'm going to misremember, Milos' The Captive Mind, which has a fantastic passage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: He was a Polish intellectual who says Americans can never imagine what it's like for civilization to be completely destroyed as it was in Poland by the end of World War II, to have no rule of law, to have no security of even person, never mind property rights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: They can't imagine what that's like and what it will lead you to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: So one reason for teaching history is to remind the lucky Generation Z members of California that civilization is a thin film and it can be destroyed remarkably easily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And to preserve civilization is a tremendous responsibility that we have. It's a huge responsibility and we must not destroy ourselves, whether it's in the name of wokeism or the pursuit of the metaverse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Preserving civilization and making it available not just to our kids, but to people we'll never know, generations ahead, that's the meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And do so by studying the lessons of history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Right. Not only studying them, but then acting on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: For me, the biggest problem is how do we apply history more effectively?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: It seems as if our institutions, including government, are very, very bad at applying history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Lessons of history are learned poorly, if at all. Analogies are drawn crudely. Often the wrong inferences are drawn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: One of the big intellectual challenges for me is how to make history more useful. And this was the kind of thing that professors used to hate, but really practically useful so that policymakers and citizens can think about the decisions that they face with a more historically informed body of knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Whether it's a pandemic, the challenge of climate change, what to do about Taiwan. I can't think of a better set of things to know before you make decisions about those things than the things that history has to offer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Well, I love the discipline of applied history. Basically going to history and saying, what are the key principles here that are applicable to the problems of today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And how can we solve that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: The great philosopher of history, R.G. Collingwood, said in his autobiography, which was published in 1939, that the purpose of history was to reconstitute past thought from whatever surviving remnants there were, and then to juxtapose it with our own predicament.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that's that juxtaposition of past experience with present experience that is so important. We don't do that well. And indeed, we've flipped it so that academic historians now think their mission is to travel back to the past with the value system of 2021 and castigate the dead for their racism and sexism and transphobia and whatnot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And that's exactly wrong. Our mission is to go back and try to understand what it was like to live in the 18th century, not to go back and condescend to the people of the past. And once we've had a better understanding, once we've seen into their lives, read their words, try to reconstitute their experience to come back and understand our own time better. That's what we should really be doing. But academic history has gone completely haywire. And it does almost the exact opposite of what I think it should do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And by studying history, walk beautifully, gracefully through this simulation, as you described by mapping the lessons of history into the world of today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: We have virtual reality already in our heads. We do not need Oculus and the metaverse. This was an incredible, hopeful conversation. And in many ways that I did not expect, I thought our conversation would be much more about history than about the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: And it turned out to be the opposite. Thank you so much for talking today. It's a huge honor to finally meet you, to talk to you. Thank you for your valuable time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Thank you, Lex, and good luck with Putin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Neil Ferguson. To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description. And now let me leave you with some words from Neil Ferguson himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niall Ferguson: History of Money, Power, War, and Truth | Lex Fridman Podcast #239

body.input: No civilization, no matter how mighty it may appear to itself, is indestructible. Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: And then when all of that is allowed to pass from your mind, you have this clear appreciation of what you really love in life, which is just like just living, just the moment.

body.input: But for the second question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: The revolt against the fundamental meaninglessness of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: Yes, exactly. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: It was what does love play? What role does love play?

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: Yeah, in the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: The way I see it, love is a reason you want to share experiences with other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: That's how I see it. Like the people you really love, you want to share the things you're going through with them.

body.input: The good and the bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: Yeah, exactly. That's my simple take on love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: My take on it is that part of what it is to be human is to be somebody who feels things emotionally, and love is one of the most intense feelings you can have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: Obviously, there's the opposite of that and there's things like hate, but I think the love you feel for people like your parents and your friends and romantic love in that moment is much more intense than in other situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Botez Sisters: Chess, Streaming, and Fame | Lex Fridman Podcast #319

body.input: And I think it's also just very unique to humans. And that's what I appreciate about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Saylor: Bitcoin, Inflation, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #276

body.input: And the purist would say we stay there. Get your Bitcoin off the exchange.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Saylor: Bitcoin, Inflation, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #276

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Saylor: Bitcoin, Inflation, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #276

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Saylor: Bitcoin, Inflation, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #276

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Saylor: Bitcoin, Inflation, and the Future of Money | Lex Fridman Podcast #276
